integrity: The structural practical-number criterion is treated as prior work. The claimed contribution is the fixed-two-prime counting phase law and its liminf/limsup constants; finite computations are not presented as proof of the asymptotic.
limitations: The theorem concerns only practical integers with exactly two distinct prime factors.
No effective numerical error term is claimed.
Finite verification is corroborative only; the asymptotic proof uses the prime number theorem.
The 1954 Stewart article was not directly inspected in full text; the exact criterion was verified in later full-text sources.
title: Dyadic phase law for practical numbers with exactly two prime factors
